prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that at the Petersons' potluck, you presented a store-bought dish in your own cookware. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts microphone, glances nervously at the gavel*

Mr. Chairman, members of the committee—

I invoke my Fifth Amendment rights against self-incrimination regarding the provenance of the seven-layer dip.

However, if the committee will permit, I wish to clarify for the record that any dish appearing in my vintage Pyrex was, at minimum, *transferred* into said Pyrex on my own property, which I believe constitutes a good-faith domestic manufacturing process under the informal bylaws of Midwest potluck culture.

*shuffles papers*

I will neither confirm nor deny that the "homemade" slow-cooker meatballs originated from a Costco bag. I will note, however, that the committee's witness—the neighbor who "saw the trays in my recycling bin"—has had a disputed claim on my rhubarb patch since 2019, and her testimony should be weighed accordingly.

*leans forward*

What I *will* say, under oath: I removed the price stickers. I sprinkled fresh parsley. I endured Mrs. Delacroix's twenty-minute story about her gallbladder surgery to secure the outlet near the buffet. These are the sacrifices that define citizenship in our community.

I am prepared to name others, Mr. Chairman. The entire dessert table was Kroger. *All of it.*

But I am not a traitor to the potluck. I am a realist.

I yield back my remaining time, and I respectfully request that my Pyrex be returned without the committee's potato salad residue still crusted in the corners.

*reclines, mops brow with paper napkin*
